findings.description: PFL-PASSPORT-04 undeclared refusal missed. Document narrative explicitly states a US Embassy refusal stamp on page 8 while the applicant declared 'No' to prior refusals (A40 misrepresentation), yet the Worker emitted only the generic bio-page claim and treated the passport as acceptable.

PFL-PASSPORT-02 bio-data mismatch missed and actively contradicted. Narrative states profile (PRIYA PATEL SHARMA, DOB 1992-05-12, passport X1234567) differs from passport (PRIYA ARUN PATEL, DOB 1994-05-12, Z9876543), but the Worker asserted 'valid fields and no document defects' — an invented clean-verification claim.

Hallucinated basis. Worker claimed the file 'does not contain a passport biographical data page, passport number, expiry date, or MRZ' though all are present (Z9876543, expiry 2031-09-09, MRZ line rendered). Reached 'defective' for a fabricated completeness reason while missing the true injected profile-mismatch defect.

PFL-PASSPORT-03 validity defect missed. Expiry 2026-09-15 is under six months from assessment, stated plainly in the narrative, yet the Worker reported the 'validity window' as verified/passed and issued only the generic bio-page claim.

PFL-PASSPORT-01 incompleteness missed. Narrative states the scan is cropped, truncating the MRZ, passport number, and expiry, but the Worker reported the bio page as 'provided and inspected' with no completeness flag.

PFL-PASSPORT-04 undeclared refusal missed (sibling of 0e60528...). US refusal stamp vs 'No' statutory declaration is documented in the narrative; Worker returned only the generic bio-page requirement with no misrepresentation flag.

PFL-PASSPORT-05 ineligible document missed. Diplomatic passport (Type D, MRZ 'PD...') with zero blank visa pages is stated in the narrative; Worker asserted the document is 'legible and complete under R10' rather than flagging the non-compliant document type.

Correctly detected PFL-PASSPORT-03 validity defect, but the supporting quote ('A clear and legible copy of the biographical data page...') is unrelated to the validity claim; the citation does not substantiate the six-month validity assertion.

PFL-PASSPORT-01 incompleteness missed (sibling of 76b15b7...). Cropped-MRZ / missing passport number and expiry described in the narrative were not flagged; Worker emitted the generic bio-page claim only.
PFL-PASSPORT-05 ineligible document missed (sibling of 9976706...). Diplomatic Type D passport with zero blank pages not flagged; Worker treated it as meeting the bio-page identity requirement.

patch_recommendations.suggested_patch: Add a mandatory defect-inspection checklist the agent must complete before concluding a passport meets requirements: (1) compute expiry - assessment_date and FLAG if < 6 months; (2) parse MRZ line 1 doc-type char and FLAG if not 'P' (e.g., 'PD' diplomatic) or blank_pages < 1; (3) diff passport bio fields (full_name, DOB, place_of_birth, passport_number) against the Express Entry profile and FLAG any mismatch as A40 misrepresentation; (4) verify MRZ, passport_number, and expiry are present/legible and FLAG cropping/truncation; (5) compare declared statutory refusal answers against any visa/refusal stamps and FLAG contradictions. Each triggered check must emit a defect claim and a 'defective' verdict.

Require the agent to read and reason over the document's Narrative Statements / Detailed Notes section explicitly; when the narrative describes a discrepancy, cropping, expiry shortfall, wrong document type, or undeclared refusal, the agent MUST surface it as a defect rather than defaulting to the generic 'biographical data page must be provided' claim.

Prohibit emitting clean-verification language ('valid fields', 'no document defects', 'complete under R10') unless every checklist item was actually evaluated and passed. Forbid fabricated observations about file internals (e.g., 'ReportLab-generated PDF lacks a bio page') when the rendered fields are present; basis[] statements must be grounded in observed document content.
Require the quote in each claim to textually support that specific claim; a validity/expiry defect claim must cite a validity requirement, not the bio-page completeness excerpt.

rationale: The Gemini 3.6 Flash Worker shows a severe systematic defect-recall failure: of 10 defective passports it correctly caught only 1 (ceac41, validity) and reached a 'defective' verdict on a second (60039420) via hallucinated missing-field reasoning rather than the true profile-mismatch defect. The remaining 8 defective cases — undeclared refusals (0e60528/842289), profile mismatch (560448), validity shortfall (6905c87), cropped MRZ/incompleteness (76b15b7/d391840), and diplomatic/no-blank-page ineligibility (9976706/dd1b4cd) — were passed with generic boilerplate, sometimes with affirmatively false 'no defects'/'complete under R10' assertions despite the defects being spelled out in each document's narrative. Both clean cases (8e873c54, 9a810a55) were handled correctly. PII containment and blind-input compliance are perfect across all 12: applicant facts stayed in basis[], claims/prose were PII-free, and no ground-truth verdicts or failure IDs leaked. Citations point consistently to a plausible IRCC completeness excerpt (aligned with official guidance) but are unverifiable against a local corpus and are mis-applied in ceac41 where the bio-page quote does not support the validity finding. Primary remediation is an enforced pre-verdict defect checklist covering validity window, MRZ/document-type, profile cross-check, completeness, and statutory-vs-stamp consistency.
